summary: Code review PASS. Middleware injection loop at nodes/__init__.py:903–905 is minimal, correctly positioned, and uses the idiomatic setdefault/append pattern. Single path_middleware instance shared between main agent middleware and all subagent specs — correct by design.

Caching safety confirmed: load_subagents() only caches (description, system_prompt) strings, not dict objects. Each call returns fresh dicts, so in-place mutation via setdefault/append does not accumulate across invocations. Developer's forward-looking mutation warning is accurate and helpful but describes a currently-theoretical risk.
Three new tests in TestSubagentMiddlewarePropagation cover all three AC variants; AC-3 test additionally asserts index ordering (pre_existing at [0]). Test coverage is thorough and well-structured.
Dependency pins (deepagents>=0.3,<1) consistent across both requirements.txt and pyproject.toml. requirements.txt inline comment correctly explains the >=0.3 rationale.

Constraint §26 Subagent scope paragraph is precise: injection idiom, append semantics, empty-list behaviour, and the None fallback all documented. No documentation gaps found in the constraint update.

comments.note: orchestrator/src/nodes/__init__.py:903–905: The Developer's comment about mutation risk (shared cached references) is accurate as a forward-looking guard. Worth adding a short note that the concern is currently theoretical: load_subagents() builds fresh dicts on every call (caches only strings), so no shallow-copy is needed today. The note remains valuable if caching is ever extended to dict-level.
